transcript.statement: Trustworthiness is crucial in autonomous driving systems to protect user data and ensure system integrity. My requirements TRU-01 (data encryption), TRU-02 (role-based access control), TRU-03 (data logging), TRU-04 (data anonymization), TRU-05 (security audits), TRU-06 (secure software updates), and TRU-07 (user consent transparency) are designed to enhance security, privacy, and accountability. These are essential to foster user trust and comply with regulatory standards. I raise conflicts with the EfficiencyAgent's EFF-03 and EFF-07 that prioritize performance during emergencies, which may compromise security protocols and data integrity.

conflicts_raised.description: Prioritizing smoothness and speed in emergency maneuvers may lead to lapses in data integrity and security measures, compromising TRU requirements.

transcript.statement: Ethical compliance is paramount for an autonomous driving system to ensure user safety and regulatory adherence. My requirements RES-01 to RES-07 establish a framework for compliance with safety reports, ensuring critical system monitoring and execution of Minimal Risk Maneuvers. I raise conflicts with TRU's emphasis on performance during emergencies (TRU-06) and the EfficiencyAgent's EFF-03 and EFF-07, as these may compromise passenger safety and compliance with safety regulations. Prioritizing smoothness or speed could lead to inadequate responses in critical situations, undermining accountability and safety measures.

conflicts_raised.description: Focusing on performance and smooth transitions during emergencies may lead to non-compliance with safety protocols and inadequate responses, risking passenger safety.

transcript.statement: Sustainability is critical for the long-term viability of autonomous driving systems. My requirements GRN-01 (energy consumption reduction), GRN-02 (renewable energy sources), GRN-03 (lifecycle assessments), GRN-04 (energy recovery efficiency), GRN-05 (carbon emissions monitoring), GRN-06 (energy-efficient routing), and GRN-07 (emergency protocols for energy minimization) are designed to ensure that we minimize environmental impacts and optimize resource usage. I raise conflicts with EfficiencyAgent's focus on speed (EFF-01) and smoothness (EFF-07) during emergency maneuvers, which may lead to increased energy consumption and undermine sustainability goals.

conflicts_raised.description: Prioritizing speed and smoothness during emergency maneuvers can lead to increased energy consumption, undermining sustainability objectives.

transcript.statement: Safety is the foremost priority in autonomous driving systems. My requirements SAF-01 to SAF-07 establish a robust framework for ensuring multi-layer safety, including passive, active, and functional safety mechanisms, along with protocols for Minimal Risk Maneuvers (SAF-02) and continuous monitoring of ODD compliance (SAF-03). I raise conflicts with EfficiencyAgent's EFF-03 and EFF-07, which may compromise safety by prioritizing performance over safety during critical maneuvers, potentially leading to hazardous situations. Additionally, the focus on minimizing jerk (SAF-04) must not be relaxed during emergencies, as passenger safety is paramount.

conflicts_raised.description: Prioritizing performance during emergency maneuvers may compromise safety protocols, risking passenger safety and undermining the execution of Minimal Risk Maneuvers.

transcript.statement: Performance efficiency is critical for the success of the autonomous driving system. My requirements EFF-01 (30% travel time reduction), EFF-02 (jerk minimization), EFF-03 (timely MRM execution), EFF-04 (100 ms ODD compliance monitoring), EFF-05 (95% optimal speed generation success), EFF-06 (non-convex constraint handling under 50 ms), and EFF-07 (smooth transitions during emergencies) are designed to enhance responsiveness and throughput while ensuring safety. I raise conflicts with SafetyAgent's SAF-04 and ResponsibilityAgent's RES-06, as strict jerk limits and prioritizing safety over performance could lead to slower responses during critical situations, potentially compromising overall system efficiency.

conflicts_raised.description: Strict jerk limits and safety prioritization during emergencies can lead to slower responses, undermining system efficiency and performance.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure a multi-layer safety architecture, including passive, active, and functional safety mechanisms, while prioritizing the execution of Minimal Risk Maneuvers during emergencies.
The system shall execute Minimal Risk Maneuvers within 5 seconds upon detecting critical failures, ensuring safety while allowing for dynamic data security adjustments.
The system shall continuously monitor Operational Design Domain compliance and issue timely human takeover requests when boundaries are approached.
The system shall maintain a jerk value below 0.5 m/s³ during normal operations and allow flexibility during emergency maneuvers for safety.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints within a response time of 100 milliseconds.
The system shall implement emergency protocols to ensure safety and data security during critical maneuvers, optimizing energy consumption.
The system shall achieve a minimum 30% reduction in average travel time compared to baseline scenarios while maintaining safety.
The system shall achieve at least a 95% success rate in optimal speed profile generation during path planning.
The system shall provide real-time monitoring of carbon emissions during operation, targeting a reduction of 25% over five years.
